title: Civic-state protest at Trg slobode, Tuzla
location: Trg slobode, Tuzla, Bosnia and Herzegovina
scope: A public gathering in Tuzla. It is a separate in-country event from diaspora gatherings and the Sarajevo OHR event; the article does not establish attendance or threshold.
participants_original: Unknown; the opened partial Anadolu report provides no count or size estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: the source confirms a public protest but reports no attendance estimate, so the ≥50 threshold is not established.

start_date.summary: Anadolu report dated Jan. 10 describes the gathering as held on that date.

end_date.summary: The partial report says the gathering ended peacefully on Jan. 10; no exact time is given.

location.summary: The report places the protest at Trg slobode in Tuzla.

scope.summary: The report describes a Tuzla public protest. It separately notes a letter read in other parts of Bosnia and Europe; those actions are not combined with this city event.

organizer.summary: The partial report names a speaker but does not identify the local organizing group; organizer remains unknown.

demands.summary: The report describes opposition to divisions and the current constitutional arrangement, calls for a normal state for all citizens, and quotes a call to the international community to change the arrangement. Domestic-policy target eligibility remains for review.

participants_original.summary: No attendee count or estimate appears in the partial report.

participants_min.summary: No numeric or qualitative lower bound is reported.

participants_max.summary: No numeric or qualitative upper bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The event is reported as a protest, but the article gives no number from which to establish at least 50 participants.

protester_violence.summary: The report explicitly describes the gathering as ending peacefully.

state_response.summary: No event-specific response by domestic state actors is reported; each response variable remains unknown.

notes: Body evidence: Anadolu Agency, partial news-feed report, lines 81–101. It says only part of the news-feed content is available. The cited call to the international community makes domestic target coding uncertain even though the substantive grievance concerns Bosnia’s constitutional arrangement.
open_questions: Did this public gathering reach 50 participants?
Does the constitutional-arrangement demand count as a domestic policy target when the quoted appeal is directed to the international community?
Are there fuller independent local reports giving organizer, attendance, or state response?

title: Gathering outside the Office of the High Representative in Sarajevo
location: Outside the Office of the High Representative (OHR), Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
scope: A Sarajevo public gathering reported outside the OHR. Keep it distinct from other Jan. 10 Sarajevo or Bosnia-wide campaign actions unless a source establishes identity.
participants_original: Search-only Vijesti.ba excerpt dated Jan. 10 at 13:00 says “several hundred” citizens gathered; body not reviewed, so this remains an unverified discovery estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: Search-only S008 excerpt says several hundred gathered outside OHR; body not reviewed. Threshold is provisionally indicated but not verified from an opened event report.

start_date.summary: Search-result evidence dates the OHR gathering to Jan. 10, 2022; event body evidence is unavailable for these cards.

location.summary: The contemporaneous headlines/snippets identify a gathering outside the OHR in Sarajevo.

scope.summary: Discovery records describe a Sarajevo gathering outside OHR. S004 independently identifies Sarajevo among wider Jan. 10 campaign sites, but does not tie its campaign-wide turnout/demands to this OHR event; it is therefore not used to merge events or code turnout.

organizer.summary: The reviewed snippets do not establish a specific organizer.

demands.summary: Search-only Tanjug-origin snippet says protesters called for sanctions against Milorad Dodik/Republika Srpska and shouted “Zaradi platu” (“Earn your pay”) toward Schmidt. The target at the venue was Christian Schmidt, Bosnia’s international High Representative; whether any demand independently targets Bosnia’s domestic government/policy for unit eligibility is unresolved.

participants_original.summary: Search-only Vijesti.ba excerpt says several hundred citizens gathered; it is not body-verified and is not attributed to an opened independent report.

participants_min.summary: The search snippet qualitatively suggests more than 50, but no body was reviewed and no numeric range is assigned.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper estimate is reported in the available snippets.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Search-only “several hundred” estimate suggests the threshold, but the body remains unread.

protester_violence.summary: No reviewed body evidence addresses protester violence; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Search snippets separately say Schmidt addressed the gathering (S008) and that he invited representatives to speak, they declined, and he spoke outside (S027). Schmidt is the international High Representative, not a domestic state actor for this target rule. No domestic-state response is established; all seven variables remain unknown.

end_date.summary: No source body or snippet establishes when the physical gathering ended.

notes: Search-only candidate. OHR is an international institution and Christian Schmidt held the international High Representative role. Preserve S027 as Tanjug-origin reporting, not independent corroboration of same-event OHR coverage. Attendance and exact interaction/demand wording remain snippet-level evidence.
open_questions: Does the demand for sanctions against Dodik/Republika Srpska count as a Bosnia domestic-policy target, or is the gathering directed solely to the international High Representative/OHR?
Can an opened report independently verify attendance and the exact demands?
What was the event-specific physical end and did any Bosnia domestic-state actor respond?

title: “Buđenje građana” protest outside the Serbian Embassy, Sarajevo
location: Outside the Embassy of Serbia, Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
scope: A peaceful public protest outside the Serbian Embassy. Reports contain demands addressed to Serbia and, separately, a domestic RS/authorities policy demand; do not merge with the Jan. 10 OHR or diaspora actions.
organizer: “Buđenje građana” (“Citizens’ Awakening”); Anadolu identifies organizer Suad Đozić and organizations/individuals around the initiative.
participants_original: Unknown; neither opened report gives an attendance estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: the reports confirm a protest but provide no participant count or estimate.

start_date.summary: Anadolu and Klix place the Sarajevo protest on Jan. 9, 2022; Anadolu was updated Jan. 10.

end_date.summary: Klix reports the protest ended at about 12:45 on Jan. 9; no exact start time appears.

location.summary: Both contemporaneous reports place the gathering outside Serbia’s Embassy in Sarajevo.

scope.summary: Two reports identify the gathering as a public protest outside a foreign embassy. They document both foreign-targeted messages and a distinct demand concerning Bosnia’s RS entity/local authorities; retain target distinction for coding review.

organizer.summary: Klix names the initiative “Buđenje građana”; Anadolu identifies organizer Suad Đozić and participating organizations/individuals.

demands.summary: Keep reports distinct. S015 (Anadolu) centers demands on Serbia: recognize the Srebrenica genocide, observe diplomatic protocol/nonparticipation in RS Day, stop imposing education programs in RS, repay for Drina hydropower, and halt dam construction absent a boundary agreement or Bosnian institutional approval. S016 (Klix) separately reports a domestic-policy demand that RS be abolished and criticism that current authorities could not/would not protect non-Serb residents. This domestic demand may satisfy the own-country target rule; the foreign-embassy venue and Serbia-directed demands remain part of the event context.

participants_original.summary: Neither opened report supplies an attendance count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric or qualitative lower bound is reported.

participants_max.summary: No numeric or qualitative upper bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reports confirm a protest but do not establish a count or estimate of at least 50 participants.

protester_violence.summary: Both reports describe a peaceful protest; Klix also reports it ended peacefully at about 12:45.

state_response.summary: Neither report gives an event-specific response by Bosnia or Serbian authorities; each of the seven response variables remains unknown.

notes: Keep source accounts distinct: S015 primarily reports demands directed to the Serbian state/officials. S016 separately records a demand that Republika Srpska be abolished and criticism that local authorities do not/will not protect non-Serb residents. The latter may establish a domestic policy target; inclusion still depends on target-rule interpretation and the unverified ≥50 threshold.
open_questions: Can independent evidence establish at least 50 participants?
Does the demand to abolish Republika Srpska and criticism of local authorities meet the domestic target criterion, despite the embassy venue and the explicit Serbian-government demands?
Are there additional contemporaneous reports that establish size or response?
